recentItems.title: 1976: The Dartford Tunnel is Skint | Nationwide | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
"Where Kent clasps Essex in a concrete handshake, ninety feet beneath the Thames."

Luke Casey reports on the second Dartford tunnel, which has been under construction for over two years at a vast cost, and is two years behind schedule. This, together with outstanding debts incurred in constructing the first tunnel, has led to the toll being doubled. The doubling of the toll has led to a reduction in traffic, which could in turn mean that there is insufficient demand for the second tunnel. What can be done?


Clip taken from Nationwide, originally broadcast on BBC One, 15 September, 1976.

recentItems.title: 1988: Life at the Football Association's School of Excellence | The Lowdown | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
The Lowdown, a documentary strand for young people, follows the progress of the latest intake of boys at the Football Association's School of Excellence at Lilleshall, Shropshire.

Each year, an initial group of over 400 players are offered trials at Lilleshall, but only 16 will be given 2-year scholarships. 14 year-olds Robert Price of Oldham Athletic, David Schoenberger of QPR and Jonathan Stanger of Manchester United are among this year's group of 16. They will spend the next two years under the tutelage of FA Technical Director Dave Sexton and England goalkeeping coach Mike Kelly. 

On top of their extensive football training, they will also have to adjust to living away from home for the first time, and studying in a new school - Idsall Comprehensive.


Clip taken from The Lowdown: On the Ball, originally broadcast on BBC One, 24 May, 1988.

recentItems.title: 1975: A Nun's Life | Tuesday Documentary | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
An examination of the world of the Nun.
Over the last ten years nuns have been directed to reconsider their attitudes to the values flowing from the three vows. Because of this they have come under enormous pressures and are in a state of anxious change.

Tonight's documentary examines the inner world of the nun to discover what happens when women answer the irresistible call to serve God in the most complete way they know.


Clip taken from Tuesday Documentary: Chastity, Poverty and Obedience, originally broadcast on BBC One, 27 May, 1975.

recentItems.title: 1980: The Microelectronics Revolution | The Silicon Factor | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
The silicon chip, unnoticed by most of us a few years ago, is now something everybody has heard about, few understand and many are beginning to fear. Is it really the basis for a revolution as profound as the industrial revolution? And what kind of revolution is it?

In this first programme, Bernard Falk takes a laymen's view of what the silicon chip is, how it s made and how it works. From a Chicago millionaire's high-tech home to a Birmingham car test-track, and from a psychiatric hospital in Scotland to a Swedish factory, he looks at how the new technology is being used and considers what it could do in the future.


Clip taken from The Silicon Factor: What's it all About?, originally broadcast on BBC One, 19 March, 1980.

recentItems.title: 1989: Flares are Back in Manchester | North West Tonight | BBC Archive
recentItems.description:
"Liverpool had the Beatles, London had Carnaby Street, Manchester is now flying the fashion heights with the flares."

North West Tonight's Bob Whittaker reports on the renewed popularity of flared trousers amongst the youth of Manchester. For now, the flares - made at Joe's denim factory in Stockport - are not available in big chain stores, they're only available in independent retailers in places like Affleck's Arcade. 

Are they about to go mainstream? What does your average Mancunian think of flares?


Clip taken from North West Tonight, originally broadcast on BBC One North West, 12 December, 1989.
